concerns.text: The SNR calculation is methodologically unsound for ERP analysis. It compares the MMN Amplitude (a mean difference across N trials) to the 'noise floor' defined as the standard deviation of the pre-stimulus baseline (raw signal noise). Because MMNs are typically buried in noise and only emerge via averaging, the raw SD is orders of magnitude larger than the mean difference. This check will likely fail for all valid data unless the denominator is the Standard Error of the Mean (SEM) or the SD of the averaged baseline.

The topographic validation is circular for the 'simple' condition. The canonical template is generated by averaging the 'simple' condition; correlating the 'simple' condition against this template measures inter-subject consistency (homogeneity), not neurophysiological validity. The plan should explicitly distinguish between the 'consistency check' (simple vs. template) and the 'validity check' (complex vs. template).
